newsitem.title: UK: UK rapist who quizzed victim in court gets life.
newsitem.headline: UK rapist who quizzed victim in court gets life.

text.p: A British rapist who triggered outrage by interrogating his victim in court for six days and making her relive every moment of the assault was sentenced on Wednesday to life imprisonment. "In my view you are a danger to women which, in the past, you have clearly demonstrated," Judge Ann Goddard told 42-year-old Ralstan Edwards, who had previous convictions for a rape and assaults on women.
During his trial in August Edwards wore exactly the same clothes as he had on when he attacked victim Julia Mason, and made her relive in minute detail the 18 hours of her ordeal.
The case provoked outrage and calls for changes to the law that allows an accused rapist to conduct his own defence.
"I have been raped twice; once in his filthy den and once in front of judge and jury in a British court of law," 34-year-old Mason said after the trial.
Edwards was found guilty on two charges of rape and was given life terms on each count.
Mason said she believed Edwards had got further gratification from being allowed to humiliate her in court.

Edwards, who made a living selling condoms to prostitutes, dismissed his lawyer on the first day of his trial. Mason was only informed that he would cross-question her on the day she entered the witness box.

In 1991, Britain withdrew the right for suspects conducting their own defence to question their alleged victims if they were children. Women's groups said they wanted the law extended to prevent them from quizzing women in cases of rape and assault.
They said they feared Mason's experience would discourage women from reporting sexual crimes because of the ordeal they may face in court.
